entries.name: Engelmann spruce
entries.leaves: evergreen, short stiff 4-sided needles
entries.flowers: no true flowers; red male and purple female cones
entries.voxel_shape: tall dense conical spire, narrow at treeline
entries.notes: The backbone of the Rocky Mountain subalpine forest; at treeline it stunts into hedges.

entries.name: Subalpine fir
entries.leaves: evergreen, flat soft needles with two white stomatal lines
entries.flowers: no true flowers; upright purple cones
entries.fruit: cylindrical cones that disintegrate on the branch
entries.voxel_shape: narrow spire, short branches, often with dead lower snags under deep snow
entries.notes: Forms dense dark stands just below treeline; boughs are the classic western subalpine look.

entries.name: Scots pine
entries.leaves: evergreen, blue-green needles in pairs
entries.flowers: no true flowers; yellow male and red female cones
entries.fire: killed by, but self-seeds after fire
entries.voxel_shape: tall straight trunk with flat-topped umbrella crown; orange upper bark
entries.notes: The iconic pine of the Caledonian pinewoods and the heathlands of the Baltic and Siberia.

entries.name: Dwarf mountain pine
entries.leaves: evergreen, dark green needles in pairs
entries.flowers: no true flowers; small cones
entries.fruit: small dark cones, often several along a shoot
entries.voxel_shape: dense low creeping bush with many tortured trunks hugging the ground
entries.notes: Grows exactly where trees should not survive: avalanche chutes and the snowline of the Alps.

entries.name: European larch
entries.leaves: deciduous needles in soft rosettes; brilliant gold in autumn
entries.flowers: no true flowers; red female cones
entries.fruit: small erect ovoid cones with persistent scales
entries.fire: partly survives; thick bark protects the trunk
entries.voxel_shape: tall straight grey trunk with open conical crown of drooping branch tiers
entries.notes: One of very few deciduous conifers; its autumn gold marks the Alpine larch forests from afar.

entries.name: Alpine larch
entries.leaves: deciduous needles; intense golden-yellow in autumn
entries.flowers: no true flowers; purple female cones
entries.fire: survives; thick bark shields the trunk
entries.voxel_shape: slender trunk with short horizontal branch whorls; autumn color is the landmark
entries.notes: Grows only in the coldest, snowiest pockets of the high cordillera; the tree that paints September gold.

entries.name: Swiss stone pine
entries.leaves: evergreen, five needles per bundle
entries.flowers: no true flowers; male cones reddish
entries.fruit: large ovoid cones with edible wingless nuts
entries.voxel_shape: broad dense green pyramid, darker and bulkier than a spruce
entries.notes: Its fat seeds are buried by nutcrackers (Nucifraga caryocatactes), which plant the next forest.

entries.name: Whitebark pine
entries.leaves: evergreen, five needles per bundle
entries.flowers: no true flowers; small dark cones
entries.fruit: cones that stay closed, releasing wingless seeds
entries.fire: killed by, but depends on open burns to regenerate
entries.voxel_shape: wind-sculpted umbrella crown, often multi-stemmed and leaning on ridgelines
uses: seed crop for Clark's nutcracker and grizzlies
entries.notes: Keystone of the high cordillera food web; its nuts feed nutcrackers, squirrels and grizzly bears.

entries.name: Great Basin bristlecone pine
entries.leaves: evergreen, five short needles per bundle, retaining for decades
entries.flowers: no true flowers; small prickly cones
entries.fire: killed by; resinous wood burns hot
entries.voxel_shape: low twisted gnarled trunk, dead white wood strips, sparse green tufts on lee side
entries.notes: Oldest known living tree species; 'Methuselah' is nearly 4,900 years old and its location is secret.

entries.name: Mountain hemlock
entries.leaves: evergreen, short stalked needles all around the twig
entries.flowers: no true flowers; small woody cones
entries.voxel_shape: drooping leader that curves like a fishing rod, dense skirt of branches
entries.notes: The wet-coast true mountain hemlock; huge snow loads and permanent moisture keep it alive.

entries.name: Deodar cedar
entries.leaves: evergreen, needles clustered on short shoots
entries.flowers: no true flowers; upright barrel cones
entries.fruit: large barrel-shaped cones that shatter when ripe
entries.voxel_shape: huge pyramidal silhouette with drooping weeping branch tips
entries.notes: The sacred devdaru of the Himalaya; its timber built the temples of the western hills.

entries.name: Himalayan blue pine
entries.leaves: evergreen, five long drooping bluish needles per bundle
entries.flowers: no true flowers; conical cones
entries.fruit: long slender resinous cones, often curved
entries.voxel_shape: broad open crown, needles hang like blue-green streamers
entries.notes: The mid-altitude pine of the Himalaya; the drooping silver-blue foliage is unmistakable.

entries.name: Common juniper
entries.leaves: evergreen, needle-like in whorls of three
entries.flowers: no true flowers; male yellow, female green cones
entries.fruit: blue-black berry-like cones, the gin spice
entries.voxel_shape: upright or spreading prickly column, often bare at the base with age
entries.notes: The only juniper native to both Eurasia and North America; everywhere on open mountain slopes.

entries.name: Tree rhododendron
entries.leaves: evergreen, dark leathery with rusty undersides
entries.flowers: red-pink bell clusters, March to May
entries.voxel_shape: rounded dense broadleaf with stunning red bloom balls above the canopy
entries.notes: The national flower of Nepal; entire Himalayan hillsides turn crimson in spring.

entries.name: Lenga
entries.leaves: deciduous, small oval beech leaves; orange-bronze in autumn
entries.flowers: no showy flowers; wind-pollinated catkins
entries.fruit: small beech nuts in spiny husks
entries.voxel_shape: south-beech columnar crown; at treeline it dwarfs into knee-high krummholz
entries.notes: The southern beech that dominates Patagonian mountain slopes; dwarfs to shin height at the windline.

entries.name: Rusty-leaved alpenrose
entries.leaves: evergreen, leaves with rusty scales underneath
entries.flowers: pink-red bell clusters, early summer
entries.voxel_shape: knee-to-waist dense evergreen mound on acidic slopes
entries.notes: Classic Alpine bloom just below treeline; every part carries grayanotoxin, nectar included.

entries.name: Bilberry
entries.leaves: deciduous, small oval green leaves on angled green stems
entries.flowers: urn-shaped pink-green blossoms, late spring
entries.fruit: dusky blue berries, stain dark purple
entries.voxel_shape: low branching shrub with angular green branches
entries.notes: The wild blueberry of European mountain heaths; stains fingers and lips purple for days.

entries.name: Cowberry
entries.leaves: evergreen, glossy oval with dark dots beneath
entries.flowers: small white-pink bells, early summer
entries.fruit: glossy red berries, keep all winter
entries.voxel_shape: low mat of shiny evergreen leaves under pines and birches
entries.notes: Lingonberry of the north; berries survive freezing on the plant and taste best after frost.

entries.name: Bearberry
entries.leaves: evergreen, thick spatula-shaped leaves
entries.flowers: white-pink urn flowers, early summer
entries.voxel_shape: creeping woody mat hugging bare rocky or sandy ground
entries.notes: A rock-hugging mat of tough leaves; grizzlies and ptarmigan treat it as a pantry shelf.

entries.name: Edelweiss
entries.leaves: deciduous, felted grey-white, wool over leaf and stem
entries.flowers: white wool bracts starring around clustered yellow disc florets, midsummer
entries.voxel_shape: short wool-covered stems with a white star at the top
entries.notes: The star of the high Alps on limestone ledges; protected everywhere it grows, do not pick.

entries.name: Purple saxifrage
entries.leaves: evergreen, tiny opposite leaves in tight cushions
entries.flowers: purple-magenta open cups, among the first after snowmelt
entries.voxel_shape: brick-red cushions and drifts of tiny purple stars on bare limestone
entries.notes: Often the first color after the snow clears; cushions can survive winters at -40C on open rock.

entries.name: Mountain avens
entries.leaves: evergreen, small wrinkled oval leaves
entries.flowers: white saucer flowers, characteristically eight petals, June-July
entries.voxel_shape: spreading mat of dark leaves spangled with white eight-petaled stars
entries.notes: An Ice Age relict; its mats mark base-rich ground where almost nothing else survives.

entries.name: Tufted hair grass
entries.leaves: evergreen to deciduous, stiff arching blades in dense tufts
entries.flowers: loose silvery panicles, midsummer
entries.voxel_shape: coarse fountain tussock of spiky blades
entries.notes: The tussock grass of damp mountain meadows and ravines almost everywhere in the north.

entries.name: Alpine lady fern
entries.leaves: deciduous fronds, finely cut, in circular rosettes
entries.flowers: spores only; no flowers
entries.voxel_shape: ring of arching lacy fronds rising from a short scaly rhizome
entries.notes: The fern of cold boulder fields and snowbeds; fronds die back cleanly when frost arrives.

entries.name: Trumpet gentian
entries.leaves: evergreen, basal rosettes of shiny oval leaves
entries.flowers: huge deep-blue trumpets rising straight from the ground, late spring
entries.voxel_shape: low rosette topped by a single enormous blue trumpet
entries.notes: The postcard gentian of Alpine meadows; its blue is the benchmark other blues fail to reach.

entries.name: Alpine pasqueflower
entries.leaves: deciduous, finely divided silky-hairy leaves
entries.flowers: large white to violet nodding bells, early summer
entries.fruit: long feathery achenes smothered in silver hairs
entries.voxel_shape: hairy stalks each topped by one open bell; seed tufts like silver smoke
entries.notes: Blooms right at snowmelt on calcareous slopes; whole plant is an irritant ranunculaceae.

entries.name: Moss campion
entries.leaves: evergreen, tiny opposite leaves in moss-like cushions
entries.flowers: dense cushions studded with pink five-petaled flowers, July
entries.voxel_shape: domed pincushion of dark green with a carpet of pink
entries.notes: Cushions grow perhaps a centimeter a year and can be centuries old; trampling scars them for good.

entries.name: Common kobresia
entries.leaves: evergreen, narrow rush-like blades in tussocks
entries.flowers: small brown spikelets, early summer
entries.voxel_shape: hard low tussocks of wiry blades on windswept ridges
entries.notes: The core sedge of the Tibetan alpine meadow and the wind-clipped ridges of Scandinavia and the Alps.

entries.name: Golden root
entries.leaves: deciduous, thick fleshy blue-green leaves on stout stems
entries.flowers: small dense yellow-green clusters, midsummer
entries.voxel_shape: low clump of thick upright reddish stems with fleshy leaves
entries.notes: A Viking-and-Sherpa tonic root, now overharvested in parts of the Alps and Siberia; grow it, don't dig it.

entries.name: Reindeer lichen
entries.leaves: pale grey-green branched podetia, no true leaves
entries.flowers: no true flowers; fruiting bodies rare
entries.fruit: tiny brown apothecia on branch tips
entries.voxel_shape: spongy pale carpet of fine branching antler-like tufts
entries.notes: The winter staple of reindeer; it takes 15-25 years to regrow after heavy grazing or fire.

entries.name: Larch bolete
entries.leaves: none; fleshy yellow porcini-like cap with pores, not gills
entries.flowers: no flowers; yellow pore surface under cap
entries.fruit: mushroom cap, sticky golden-orange, ring on stalk
entries.voxel_shape: classic stout mushroom: round yellow-orange cap, pale ringed stalk
entries.notes: Grows only in partnership with larch; where larch lenses gold in autumn, this mushroom follows.

entries.name: Alpine forget-me-not
entries.leaves: evergreen, tiny silvery hairy leaves in cushions
entries.flowers: sky-blue forget-me-not blossoms no bigger than a fingernail, high summer
entries.voxel_shape: a fingertip-wide downy cushion spangled with tiny blue stars
entries.notes: Once sold in florists' windows in Victorian times; now a rare jewel of high granite ridges.

entries.name: Dwarf arctic willow
entries.leaves: deciduous, coin-sized rounded leaves lying flat on the ground
entries.flowers: discreet red male and green female catkins
entries.voxel_shape: a carpet of coin-sized leaves just above the soil crust, wider than tall
entries.notes: Arguably the smallest woody plant on Earth; a treeline relative barely an inch high.

entries.name: Queñua de altura
entries.leaves: evergreen, small thick three-leaflet leaves, resinous
entries.flowers: tiny greenish hanging flowers, 5-8 mm wide
entries.voxel_shape: gnarled multi-trunked shrub-tree with peeling red bark, shrinking to a bush on the highest ridges
entries.notes: The highest-living tree in the world, recorded at 5,013 m; survives nights below -20C in thin air.

entries.name: Yareta
entries.growth: extremely slow, about 1.5 cm per year
entries.leaves: evergreen, tiny leaves in an extremely dense chartreuse cushion
entries.flowers: tiny pink or lavender hermaphrodite flowers, pollinated by flies and small wasps
entries.fire: burns hot; traditional fuel, now illegal to harvest
entries.voxel_shape: hemispherical chartreuse mound that can reach 6 m across and outlast empires
entries.notes: A cushion plant of the puna estimated at over 3,000 years old; its own density is its survival strategy.

entries.name: Kilimanjaro giant groundsel
entries.leaves: evergreen, giant spiral leaf rosette, leaves close at night (nyctinasty)
entries.flowers: large yellow composite cluster every few to many years
entries.voxel_shape: candelabra-shaped stem topped with a huge green rosette, wrapped in dead leaves
entries.notes: Equatorial alpine giant storing water and antifreeze polysaccharides; dead leaf armor insulates the stem.

entries.name: Rock tripe
entries.leaves: dark grey-brown umbilicus-fastened leaf rosettes on bare rock
entries.flowers: no flowers; rare fruiting bodies
entries.fruit: small black apothecia on leaf surface
entries.voxel_shape: rivets or small dark leathery leaves literally suction-cupped to bare rock
uses: survival food (soaked, boiled, eaten as mush)
entries.notes: Named by starving explorers who ate it, reluctantly; the taste is exactly as memorable as the name.

entries.name: Brahma Kamal
entries.leaves: deciduous, large oblong leaves in basal rosettes
entries.flowers: purple flower heads hidden in yellow-green papery bracts, July-September
entries.voxel_shape: low leaf rosette with a pale bract-wrapped bud like a green lotus
entries.notes: Blooms at 3,700-4,600 m only in high summer; gathered for temples, so populations are shrinking.
